lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Esther tells how a Jewish orphan becomes queen of Persia, Haman plots to destroy the Jews, Esther and Mordecai act, the plot is reversed, and the feast of Purim is established. The name of God does not appear in the book.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the book of Esther from Vashti's removal to the feast of Purim?
ev: Say who the main people are: Ahasuerus, Esther, Mordecai and Haman
Say what the feast of Purim remembers

nodes.d: Ahasuerus holds a great feast in Shushan; when he commands Queen Vashti to appear before the guests she refuses, and on the advice of Memucan she is removed and a decree goes out in the king's name that every man should rule in his own house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Vashti lost her place as queen?
ev: Say what Vashti refused to do and what followed (1:10-19)
Say how the king proclaimed the decree (1:20-22)

nodes.d: The king's servants gather beautiful young women to Shushan; Mordecai, a Benjamite carried away with Jeconiah, has raised his cousin Hadassah (Esther), who finds favour, is made queen in Vashti's place, and keeps her people secret at Mordecai's charge.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Esther came to be queen and what she kept secret?
ev: Say who Mordecai was and how he was related to Esther (2:5-7)
Say what Mordecai told her not to reveal (2:10)

nodes.d: Mordecai sits in the king's gate and learns that two chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, plan to kill the king; he tells Esther, who tells the king in Mordecai's name, and the matter is written in the book of the chronicles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Mordecai saved the king's life?
ev: Say who was plotting and how the king learned of it (2:21-22)
Say where it was recorded (2:23)

nodes.t: Haman plots to destroy the Jews
nodes.d: King Ahasuerus promotes Haman the Agagite, and when Mordecai will not bow to him Haman seeks to destroy all the Jews in the kingdom; lots are cast, he offers the king silver, and the king gives him his ring so a decree is sent to all the provinces that the Jews be destroyed on a set day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Haman wanted to destroy the Jews and what he persuaded the king to do?
ev: Say why Haman wanted to destroy the Jews (3:5-6)
Say what the king did and what the decree ordered (3:10-13)

nodes.d: The Jews mourn the decree; Mordecai tells Esther through Hatach to go to the king, saying deliverance will arise from another place and asking who knows whether she came to the kingdom for such a time as this. Esther asks the Jews to fast three days and says she will go in to the king, and if she perishes, she perishes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Mordecai asked Esther to do and how she answered?
ev: Say what Mordecai asked Esther to do (4:8, 13-14)
Say what Esther decided (4:15-16)

nodes.d: Esther stands in the inner court and the king holds out his sceptre to her; at her banquet she asks that the king and Haman come again the next day. Haman, angered by Mordecai, accepts his wife's advice and has a high gallows made for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when Esther went to the king and what Haman planned?
ev: Say what the king did when Esther came uninvited (5:2)
Say what Haman prepared for Mordecai (5:14)

nodes.d: The king cannot sleep and has the records read; he learns Mordecai was never rewarded and asks Haman what to do for the man the king delights to honour, and Haman, thinking it is himself, describes royal robes and a horse; he is made to lead Mordecai through the city.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Haman ended up honouring Mordecai?
ev: Say what the king learned from the records (6:1-3)
Describe what Haman had to do for Mordecai (6:10-11)

nodes.d: At the second banquet Esther asks the king for her life and her people, who have been sold to be destroyed, and names Haman as the enemy; the king in his wrath has Haman hanged on the gallows Haman prepared for Mordecai.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Esther revealed Haman's plot to the king?
ev: Say what Esther asked and whom she named (7:3-6)
Say how Haman died (7:9-10)

nodes.d: The king gives Haman's house to Esther and Mordecai his ring; Esther begs him to reverse Haman's letters, and since a decree cannot be revoked he permits Mordecai to write a new decree allowing the Jews to gather and defend their lives on the appointed day. Mordecai goes out in royal apparel and there is joy among the Jews.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the king made a way for the Jews to defend themselves?
ev: Say what the new decree allowed (8:11)
Say how the Jews responded (8:15-17)

nodes.d: On the thirteenth of Adar the Jews gather and overcome those who hated them; the rulers help them for fear of Mordecai, Haman's ten sons are killed, and in Shushan they have a second day, but the text repeats that they did not take the spoil. They rest and feast on the fourteenth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened on the day the Jews' enemies expected to destroy them?
ev: Say what happened on the thirteenth of Adar (9:1-5)
Say what the text notes about the spoil (9:10, 15-16)

nodes.t: The feast of Purim is established
nodes.d: Mordecai writes to the Jews in all the provinces to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar yearly as days of feasting, gladness, sending portions and gifts to the poor; they are called Purim after Pur, the lot Haman cast, and Esther and Mordecai confirm it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Purim remembers and how it is kept?
ev: Say why the feast is called Purim (9:24-26)
List what the Jews were to do on these days (9:22)

nodes.d: King Ahasuerus lays a tribute on the land and the sea; the book ends by saying Mordecai the Jew was next to the king, great among the Jews, seeking the wealth of his people and speaking peace to all his seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how the book of Esther ends and how it describes Mordecai?
ev: Say how Mordecai is described (10:3)
Say whose welfare he sought

nodes.d: Jehoiakim serves Nebuchadnezzar, then rebels, and the LORD sends bands against Judah as he said by the prophets because of Manasseh's sin; his son Jehoiachin surrenders to Babylon and Nebuchadnezzar carries off the temple treasures and about ten thousand captives. He appoints Zedekiah king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Babylon took the first captives from Judah?
ev: Say why the LORD sent the invaders (24:2-4)
Say what Nebuchadnezzar took and who he made king (24:13-17)

nodes.d: Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes, prays and returns to Jerusalem to rebuild its wall in fifty-two days despite opposition (chs. 1-7), then the law is read, the feast of booths is kept, the people confess and covenant (chs. 8-10), and the city is repopulated, the wall dedicated and abuses corrected (chs. 11-13).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Nehemiah, from the prayer in Susa to the reforms at the end?
ev: Name the main parts: building the wall, reading the law and covenant, dedication and reforms
Say who Nehemiah was and what he did for Jerusalem
